name: E2E KV Store - Voluntary Leave, Then You Must Be Let Back In
description:
Tests the cycle: voluntary `leave_group` (publishes `MemberLeft`) → self-rejoin via `join_subgroup_inheritance` is REJECTED → admin re-add puts them back in the member list.
It stops there on purpose. It does NOT assert that the re-added leaver can write again, because today they cannot — a pre-existing gap in the leave → admin-readd path that has nothing to do with re-entry control, documented at the foot of this file. The write-after-re-add property is already covered by the two kick flows.
Leaving is not a ban: node-2 can come back. What it cannot do is let ITSELF back in. `MemberLeft` writes a re-entry block, and re-entry has to be an explicit act — a freshly issued invitation, or an admin re-adding you. Inheritance is neither: an Open subgroup admits any parent member holding `CAN_JOIN_OPEN_SUBGROUPS` automatically, so if inheritance could readmit a leaver, walking out and walking back in would be indistinguishable from never having left. The only lever an admin would have left is revoking `CAN_JOIN_OPEN_SUBGROUPS` wholesale — which also bars them from every *other* Open subgroup.
The deny-list and the re-entry block are different things and this flow leans on the difference. The deny-list *silences* node-2 (its state deltas are dropped at the receive filter) and is retracted the moment any member row is written. The block *authorizes*, and deliberately survives a member-row write, so the re-join fails instead of quietly succeeding.
Direct-row prerequisite: the `leave_group` handler at `crates/context/src/handlers/leave_group.rs` requires the leaver to be a *direct* member of the subgroup (an inherited-only member has no row to remove and the handler bails with "leave the parent group where the membership anchor lives instead"). So the test admin first adds node-2 via `add_group_members` to give them a direct row. Its inherited path stays fully intact afterwards — node-2 still holds `CAN_JOIN_OPEN_SUBGROUPS` and the subgroup is still `Open` — which is what makes the rejection in Phase 5 a tight test of the block itself rather than of some incidental loss of authority.
Distinct from siblings:
  * `group-leave-context.yml` covers `leave_context` (local opt-out,
    no DAG op) → `join_context` rejoin. No `MemberLeft`, no
    deny-list, no re-entry block, no inheritance.
  * `group-kick-and-rejoin-keyshare.yml` covers `MemberRemoved`
    (admin kick), where the block is stricter still: no invitation
    readmits a removed member, only an admin re-add.
  * This workflow covers `MemberLeft` (self-published), where a
    fresh invitation WOULD also work — the invitation half of that
    is unit-tested in `governance-store`; here we exercise the admin
    re-add at the wire level.

Mero-chat user-visible failure mode this guards against: "I left a public channel and immediately rejoined myself — leaving does not actually do anything."

Each of the original scenario's nodes is an account here; see merobox/cloud_v2/port.py for the mapping.

wait_for_sync x4: replication is synchronous: a read sees every committed write

steps.name: Admin adds node-2 and node-3 to subgroup directly
Admin adds node-2 and node-3 to subgroup directly
Node-1 creates context inside Open subgroup
steps.app_name: Node-1 creates context inside Open subgroup

steps.name: Wait for MemberAdded + ContextRegistered to propagate
Confirm node-2 absent from subgroup membership
Post-leave — node-2 attempts write (must fail or be dropped)
Drain in-flight gossip before negative-control read
Negative control — node-3 must NOT see the dropped write
Assert dropped value is genuinely absent on node-3 BEFORE rejoin
Node-2 attempts to re-inherit into the subgroup (must be rejected)
Confirm subgroup membership after the rejected re-inheritance
Assert the leaver is still out
Admin (node-1) re-adds node-2 to the subgroup
Confirm subgroup membership shape after the re-add
Assert the re-added leaver is back in the member list
Assert the re-added leaver's write reached node-3
